findings.title: ENABLED_FAMILIES still gates backend bundle operations
findings.why_it_matters: The stated intent of this change is to remove enabled_families gating and derive authorability from the normalized registry contract. app.py no longer injects enabled_families into the API response, and workbench.js now gates UI via isTemplateActionAuthorable(). However, service.py still imports ENABLED_FAMILIES (line 35) and uses it at five call sites: create_bundle (line 1302), workbench_create_blank_session (line 2806), a second check in bundle context (line 2866), bundle verify (line 3575), and bundle commit/payload (line 3627). Currently ENABLED_FAMILIES = {'player', 'attack', 'plydie'} matches the authorable prefix_catalog entries exactly, so no functional regression today. But the frontend UI now says an action is authorable using the registry contract, while the backend enforces a separate hardcoded set. If a new authorable prefix is added to the registry and prefix_catalog.authorable=true but ENABLED_FAMILIES is not updated, the frontend will show the action as authorable, the user will attempt it, and the backend will return a 422 phase_not_enabled error. This is a correctness split between the two authority sources.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace ENABLED_FAMILIES checks in service.py with registry-based authorability lookups (e.g., check prefix_catalog[family].authorable or skin_family_scope[skin_family].authorable). The normalized registry is already loaded at call time via load_template_registry(). Alternatively document explicitly that ENABLED_FAMILIES is the intentional backend gate and update it in lockstep with prefix_catalog.

findings.title: Linkage check skipped when templateSetKey is empty
findings.why_it_matters: In isTemplateActionAuthorable(), the check at line 7019 guards the template_actions linkage verification with `if (templateActions.length && templateSetKey)`. If state.templateSetKey is falsy (empty string or null), the entire linkage check is skipped even when the prefix_catalog has a non-empty template_actions array. This means any prefix with template_actions defined would pass as authorable regardless of which (or no) template set is active. In the current application flow getEnabledActions() is only called after state.templateSetKey is set, making this fail-open benign at runtime. However, getEnabledActions() is also called from areAllEnabledBundleActionsReady() and getNextIncompleteBundleActionKey() without a templateSetKey guard, so if state is partially initialized the skip fires. A prefix that should only be linked to specific template sets would incorrectly appear authorable in any template set context.
findings.suggested_fix: Change the guard to: `if (templateActions.length) { if (!templateSetKey) return false; ... }` — fail-closed when templateSetKey is unknown rather than bypassing the linkage check.

findings.title: skin_family_scope absent on ts yields fail-open scope check
findings.why_it_matters: When ts.skin_family_scope is not an array (missing field or non-array value), templateScope is set to null. The guard `if (templateScope && templateScope.size && !templateScope.has(skinFamily))` then skips the scope restriction entirely — any skinFamily passes. This is fail-open: a template set without a skin_family_scope field restricts no family. The current registry always includes skin_family_scope arrays for all template sets, so no breakage today. But if a future template set is added to the JSON without the field, or if the backend returns an older schema version, every family would be treated as in-scope for that template set.
findings.suggested_fix: Treat a null templateScope (missing field) as a non-restrictive scope (current intent, acceptable) — but document this explicitly. Alternatively, treat missing skin_family_scope as fail-closed (return false) for strictness. If the intent is that missing scope == unrestricted, add a comment and add a test that verifies this behavior explicitly.

findings.title: prefix_catalog drift check compares raw vs normalized sha fields
findings.why_it_matters: In _normalize_template_registry(), the drift check (lines 1070-1077) compares fields from `ps` (a dict copy of the raw prefix_catalog entry) against fields from `action_spec` (the already-normalized action dict). For the `preview_xp_sha256` field, if the action had no explicit preview_xp_sha256 and used the l0_ref fallback in _normalize_template_action_spec(), the normalized action_spec['preview_xp_sha256'] would hold the l0_ref_sha256 value. But ps.get('preview_xp_sha256') reads the raw prefix_catalog entry, which may have an explicit preview_xp_sha256 field set to the same l0_ref_sha256 value — causing a match. However, if the prefix_catalog entry omits preview_xp_sha256 entirely (raw value empty string via `str(ps.get('preview_xp_sha256') or '').strip()`), but the normalized action has it filled from fallback, the drift check produces a false alarm: prefix='', action='abc...' mismatch even though there is no real drift. In the current registry all entries have explicit preview_xp_sha256 so this path is not triggered. This is a latent correctness gap that would fire during a v1-to-v2 migration where preview_xp_sha256 is absent from prefix_catalog but present in the normalized action.
findings.suggested_fix: Normalize `ps` through _resolve_preview_xp_fields() before the drift comparison, or explicitly skip the preview_xp/preview_xp_sha256 comparison for prefix entries that don't have those fields (using the same fallback logic). Alternatively, require preview_xp_sha256 as a mandatory explicit field in prefix_catalog entries (no fallback allowed there).

service.py line 1072: action_value = str(action_spec.get(field) or '').strip() — action_spec is normalized

findings.title: Test fixture assertion verifies inequality, not correct fallback value
findings.why_it_matters: test_normalize_action_spec_preview_xp_fallback_to_l0_ref() at line 142 asserts `result['preview_xp_sha256'] != spec['preview_xp_sha256']`. This checks the fallback sha256 differs from the original preview_xp_sha256 field, which passes only because _VALID_SPEC has 'abc123' for preview_xp_sha256 and 'def456' for l0_ref_sha256, and the test removes preview_xp. The assertion should instead positively verify `result['preview_xp_sha256'] == spec['l0_ref_sha256']` — i.e., the fallback produces the expected value. The current assertion is an accidental pass: if someone changed the fixture so both sha256 values were the same string, the assertion would pass even if the fallback logic were broken.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace line 142: `assert result['preview_xp_sha256'] != spec['preview_xp_sha256']` with `assert result['preview_xp_sha256'] == spec['l0_ref_sha256']` to pin the actual expected fallback value.

findings.title: load_template_registry cache not reset between tests
findings.why_it_matters: test_template_registry_actions_are_normalized() (line 18), test_template_registry_reference_paths_exist() (line 39), and test_template_registry_mounted_scope_is_explicit() (line 52) all call load_template_registry() directly without resetting the global _template_registry cache via _reset_template_registry_cache(). This means if test_normalize_template_registry_rejects_prefix_catalog_sha_drift() (line 145) runs before them — which patches the in-memory registry — those tests may see the patched or stale registry. The test on line 145 calls _normalize_template_registry(registry) which does NOT mutate the global cache, so the risk is actually low. However, test_normalize_registry_missing_file_returns_schema_version_2 (line 154) correctly calls _reset_template_registry_cache() in both setup and finally. The earlier integration tests that call load_template_registry() directly without reset are vulnerable to cache state from any prior test that patched _template_registry.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a pytest fixture with autouse=True or a conftest.py fixture that calls _reset_template_registry_cache() before/after each test in this module, or add explicit _reset_template_registry_cache() calls at the top of each test that calls load_template_registry().

tests/test_template_registry_schema.py line 39: same
tests/test_template_registry_schema.py line 52: same
tests/test_template_registry_schema.py lines 157-164: only test that correctly wraps with _reset_template_registry_cache()

residual_risks: ENABLED_FAMILIES in service.py is now a shadow gate that is not derived from the registry. If the registry adds a new authorable prefix and ENABLED_FAMILIES is not updated in lockstep, the frontend will appear to allow the action but all backend bundle endpoints will reject it with 422 phase_not_enabled. This split-authority risk is the most significant consequence of the partial migration.

The templateScope fail-open behavior (null when field is missing) means that any template set added to the registry without skin_family_scope will be treated as unrestricted scope for all families, potentially exposing non-authorable families in the UI.
The drift check between prefix_catalog and normalized action specs only fires at load time (startup). A registry file that drifts between the two representations after boot is not re-validated.

The compat alias spec['family'] = filename_prefix in _normalize_template_action_spec means downstream code reading 'family' will now get the filename_prefix value, which was also the case before (family WAS filename_prefix). But if a future spec has a skin_family that differs from filename_prefix, the alias may confuse family-keyed lookups in _load_reference_l0 and _load_reference_l1 which search by family value.
testing_gaps: No test verifies that the frontend isTemplateActionAuthorable() returns false when state.templateSetKey is empty/null but prefixSpec.template_actions is non-empty (linkage bypass scenario).
No backend test covers the case where a prefix_catalog entry has authorable=true but is not in ENABLED_FAMILIES — verifying whether bundle creation would still be blocked by the backend gate.
No test exercises the preview_xp_sha256 fallback path in the drift check (prefix_catalog entry lacking explicit preview_xp_sha256 while action spec acquired it via fallback).

test_templates_api_exposes_normalized_contract uses the client fixture and calls load_template_registry() through the API, but does not reset cache before the test — the 'enabled_families' absence assertion could pass even if the removal was reverted if the cached registry was loaded without that key.

The test at line 142 only verifies sha inequality rather than the exact expected fallback value, so it would not catch a regression where the fallback produced a wrong value that still differs from 'abc123'.
